title: UNT Jazz Drum Set: Self-Study BM

untCourses: Pre-audition preparation (UNT requires students below Level 1 to pass Deficient barriers first)
semesters.theme: Hands, time, and reading. Get to audition-ready basics.
goals: Play steady time with a click without drifting
Read quarter, eighth, and simple syncopated rhythms
Play a basic jazz ride pattern with hi-hat on 2 and 4
Know the form of a 12-bar blues

items.text: Matched grip, fulcrum, and rebound on a practice pad (check in a mirror)
Four basic strokes: full, down, tap, up. 5 min daily, quarter = 60-80
Single strokes (RLRL) eighth notes, 60 to 100 bpm
Double strokes (RRLL) eighth notes, 60 to 90 bpm
Kit setup: throne height, pedal and cymbal positions, basic tuning
Eighth-note rock groove, 70 to 110 bpm, 2 min unbroken with click
Bass drum variations: 8 patterns from Syncopation (Reed) bass drum studies or similar
One-bar fills on snare and toms that land on beat 1 cleanly
Click on 2 and 4 only: feel it as the backbeat for 1 minute
Count out loud: quarters, eighths, rests, ties (1 e & a)
Syncopation (Reed): first quarter- and eighth-note reading lessons on snare, 60-80 bpm
Stick Control (Stone) p.5 exercises 1-12 at 80 bpm
Rudiments: paradiddle, flam, drag, five-stroke roll, slow and even
Jazz ride pattern (spang-spang-a-lang) with hi-hat on 2 and 4, 100-140 bpm
Feather the bass drum on all 4 beats (barely audible)
Play time through a 12-bar blues play-along, counting bars out loud
Trade 4s: 4 bars time, 4 bars simple fill, keep the form

musicianship.text: Learn note names on the treble and bass clef (musictheory.net lessons)
Learn the major scale construction (W-W-H-W-W-W-H)
Learn song form: 12-bar blues and 32-bar AABA

listening: Miles Davis, Kind of Blue (Jimmy Cobb)
Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers, Moanin' (Art Blakey)
Count Basie, The Atomic Mr. Basie (Sonny Payne)

jury.text: Rock groove, 100 bpm, 2 min with click, with a fill every 8 bars
Jazz time over 3 choruses of blues at 120 bpm with a play-along, no lost form
Singles, doubles, paradiddles on pad at 90 bpm eighth notes
Read one Syncopation (Reed) page at 70 bpm without stopping
Record the jury and keep the video in your log

untCourses: MUTH 1400/1500 Theory I + Aural Skills I
semesters.theme: The ride cymbal is the center of the band.
goals: Steady swing time from 80 to 180 bpm
Basic comping on snare and bass drum
Hear and keep form on blues and AABA tunes

items.text: Ride pattern alone with click on 2 and 4, 80 to 180 bpm: even, swung, relaxed
Add hi-hat 2 and 4 plus feathered bass drum
Listen and copy: play along with 'So What' (Jimmy Cobb) and 'Moanin'' (Blakey)
Syncopation (Reed) syncopation lessons read on snare under ride and hi-hat, 100-140 bpm
Same exercises read on bass drum under ride and hi-hat
John Riley, The Art of Bop Drumming: first comping exercises
Medium-swing brush pattern (sweep plus 2 and 4 pat), 100-140 bpm
Bossa nova: cross-stick clave, bass drum 1 and 3 pattern, 120-160 bpm
Basic samba on the kit (Ed Soph Big Band Primer or similar), 80-100 bpm half-note feel
Two-bar fills in swing that set up beat 1
Trade 4s over blues and AABA, keep your place in the form
Wilcoxon, The All-American Drummer: solos 1-5 on pad
Stick Control p.5-7 exercises 1-24 at 100 bpm

musicianship.text: Theory I: intervals, major and minor scales, triads
Aural I: sing major scale and intervals up to a 5th
Keyboard I: C, F, G major scales hands separately
Sing the melody of each tune while playing time
Transcribe: write out 8 bars of Jimmy Cobb's ride and comping on 'So What'

listening: Miles Davis, Milestones (Philly Joe Jones)
Sonny Rollins, Saxophone Colossus (Max Roach)
Oscar Peterson, Night Train (Ed Thigpen, brushes)

jury.text: Swing time at 100, 140, and 180 bpm, 2 choruses each
Comp from a Syncopation page at 120 bpm
Brushes, medium swing, 2 choruses
Bossa nova and samba grooves, 16 bars each
Trade 4s over a full tune with a play-along
Sight-read a short snare etude

untCourses: MUTH 1600/1700 Theory II + Aural Skills II
semesters.theme: Big band drumming and the shuffle family.
goals: Read a big band chart and set up figures

items.text: Syncopation (Reed) shuffle and triplet exercises (UNT assigns p.10 here), 80-120 bpm
Texas shuffle and half-time shuffle grooves
Stick Control triplet section, 80 bpm
Short vs long figures: how to play each on the kit
Set-ups: one-beat and two-beat setups into ensemble hits
Ed Soph, Big Band Primer (or Steve Houghton, Studio and Big Band Drumming): read 3 charts
Play along with a Basie recording reading the chart
Ballad brushes: circular sweep at 50-70 bpm
Up-tempo ride: push from 180 to 220 bpm, relaxed
Two-feel vs four-feel: switch on the bridge
Bembe bell pattern in 6/8 with bass drum and hi-hat
Clave: son and rumba, 2-3 and 3-2
Wilcoxon All-American Drummer solos 6-12

musicianship.text: Theory II: diatonic seventh chords, chord symbols, ii-V-I
Aural II: identify maj7, m7, dom7 by ear
Keyboard II: ii-V-I shell voicings (root, 3rd, 7th) in C, F, Bb
Transcribe: Philly Joe Jones 4-bar trades on a Miles tune

listening: Count Basie, Basie Straight Ahead (Harold Jones)
Thad Jones/Mel Lewis Orchestra, Consummation (Mel Lewis)
Duke Ellington, Ellington at Newport (Sam Woodyard)

jury.text: Read and play a big band chart with a recording
Swing time at 220 bpm, 2 choruses
Shuffle groove and ballad brushes
6/8 Afro-Cuban groove with clave
Sight-read a short big band excerpt

untCourses: MUJS 2400/2410 Jazz Theory III + Aural Skills III
semesters.theme: Independence and melodic soloing. Add funk and gospel.
goals: Solo over the form of a tune
Funk ghost notes and linear grooves

items.text: Riley, Art of Bop Drumming: snare/bass drum coordination studies
Wilcoxon rudimental patterns with feet added (UNT pairs Wilcoxon with foot patterns here)
Hi-hat on all 4 beats and on 1 and 3 variations
Solo over 12-bar blues keeping the form, singing the melody in your head
Motif development: take one 2-beat idea and vary it for a chorus
Transcribe and play Max Roach trades on 'Blues Walk' (Clifford Brown and Max Roach)
Jazz waltz ride pattern and comping, 120-180 bpm
Songo groove (Soph Big Band Primer or Malabe/Weiner, Afro-Cuban Rhythms for Drumset)
Samba with brushes
Ghost notes: 16th-note grooves with accented backbeat, 80-100 bpm
Purdie shuffle (half-time triplet ghost groove)
Linear grooves (David Garibaldi, Future Sounds: first section)
Gospel basics: 6-stroke roll as a fill around the kit

musicianship.text: Jazz Theory III: chord-scale relationships, modes, tritone substitution
Aural III: sing roots of a ii-V-I, hear the bridge of rhythm changes
Improv I: learn and sing 3 bebop heads by memory
Keyboard III: shell voicings in all 12 keys (slowly)

listening: Clifford Brown and Max Roach, Study in Brown (Max Roach)
Bill Evans, Sunday at the Village Vanguard (Paul Motian)
Tower of Power, Tower of Power (David Garibaldi)

jury.text: Solo one chorus over blues and one over AABA, form intact
Jazz waltz with comping, 2 choruses
Songo and samba with brushes
One funk groove with ghost notes, one linear groove
Play the Max Roach transcription with the record

untCourses: MUJS 2500/2510 Jazz Theory IV + Aural Skills IV
semesters.theme: The sophomore checkpoint. Odd meters and jazz history.
goals: Know the drummers who shaped each jazz era

items.text: 5/4 swing: play 'Take Five' with the record
7/4 as 4+3 and 3+4, swing and straight
Count and sing the subdivisions while playing
John Riley, Beyond Bop Drumming: broken-time studies
Comp in response to a soloist (play-along with a horn solo)
Up-tempo: 220 to 260 bpm, lighter touch
New Orleans and swing: Baby Dodds, Chick Webb, Jo Jones
Bebop: Kenny Clarke, Max Roach, Roy Haynes
Hard bop and post-bop: Art Blakey, Philly Joe Jones, Elvin Jones, Tony Williams
Play 8 bars in each drummer's style
Steve Gadd and Bernard Purdie-style grooves
Wilcoxon, Modern Rudimental Swing Solos: 2 solos
Transcribe Art Blakey's solo on 'Moanin''

musicianship.text: Jazz Theory IV: reharmonization basics, modal harmony
Aural IV: hear form changes and key changes in a tune
Improv II: sing a 2-chorus solo over blues
History: build a 20-track timeline playlist, one drummer per track

listening: Dave Brubeck, Time Out (Joe Morello)
Miles Davis, Four and More (Tony Williams)
John Coltrane, Coltrane's Sound (Elvin Jones)

jury.text: Sophomore checkpoint: 15-min program with 3 contrasting tunes
Swing time at 260 bpm
5/4 and 7/4 grooves with fills
Play the Blakey transcription with the record
Explain and demonstrate 3 drummers' styles

semesters.theme: Polyrhythm, recording yourself, and leading a combo.
goals: Record and mix a trio play-along

items.text: Triplets split between hands and feet in swing
3-over-4 polyrhythm: dotted quarter on ride over swing
Transcribe one chorus of Elvin Jones comping on 'Crescent'
Set up a DAW (GarageBand, Reaper, or Logic)
Mic the kit: 2-4 mics (overheads plus kick)
Record and mix yourself with a trio play-along
Count-offs at any tempo, steady from the first beat
Common intros and endings (tag, vamp, Basie ending)
Play with real musicians: join a jam session or community band
Fast singles and doubles around the kit (sextuplets)
Hand-foot combinations (RLK, RLRLKK)
Gospel shed-style fills inside a groove, musically placed

musicianship.text: Advanced Improv I: sing and play rhythm of a famous horn solo
Arranging I: write a lead sheet arrangement of a blues with intro and ending
Write a drum chart for your arrangement
Lecture series: watch 3 drummer clinics and take notes

listening: John Coltrane, Crescent (Elvin Jones)
Herbie Hancock, Maiden Voyage (Tony Williams)
Kirk Franklin and gospel drum shed videos (gospel chops vocabulary)

jury.text: Play the Elvin transcription with the record
Submit a recorded and mixed trio track
Lead a tune with your own intro and ending
Demonstrate 3-over-4 in time
A musical 16-bar gospel chops feature

untCourses: MUMH 3520 Issues in Western Music History
semesters.theme: Modern jazz and progressive metal: odd groupings and illusions.

items.text: 7/8, 9/8, and 11/8 grooves with different groupings
Solo over a vamp in 7/8
Play along with a prog track (Tool 'Schism' or Dream Theater)
Gavin Harrison, Rhythmic Illusions: first chapters
Polymeter: groupings of 5 or 7 over 4/4 (Meshuggah-style)
Metric modulation: swing quarter to dotted-quarter pulse
Study Brian Blade, Bill Stewart, Jeff 'Tain' Watts
Transcribe 16 bars from a modern drummer of your choice
Afro-Cuban: Mozambique and cascara with clave
Bass drum endurance: 16ths at 100-140 bpm (double pedal if you have one)
Heel-toe or slide technique basics
Hi-hat foot splashes and patterns under grooves

musicianship.text: Advanced Improv II: compose a drum solo with a clear shape
Arranging II: write an original tune (lead sheet)
Music history: how rhythm in Western music shaped jazz and rock

listening: Joshua Redman, Wish (Billy Higgins) and Brian Blade Fellowship
Branford Marsalis, Crazy People Music (Jeff 'Tain' Watts)
Porcupine Tree, Fear of a Blank Planet (Gavin Harrison)

jury.text: Grooves and fills in 7/8, 9/8, 11/8
Demonstrate a polymeter and a metric modulation
Perform your original tune (with play-along or band)
Play the modern drummer transcription
Mozambique groove with clave

untCourses: MUJS 3800 Jazz Conducting and Ensemble Techniques
goals: Fluent in every style from the past 7 semesters
Pick and arrange the senior recital program

items.text: Tune the kit for jazz and for funk; record both
Dynamics: play every groove at pp, mf, ff
Choose and describe your cymbal sound
Run every jury from S0 to S6 once; note weak spots
Fix the 3 weakest items
Swing at 300 bpm (stretch goal)
Run a rehearsal: give tempos, cues, and feedback
Conduct (or count off and cue) a big band chart
Record a 3-song demo in 3 styles
Choose 6-8 recital tunes and write set notes

musicianship.text: Conducting: basic beat patterns in 2, 3, 4
Arrange 2 recital tunes for your band

listening: Chris Dave, Robert Glasper Experiment, Black Radio
Antonio Sanchez, Migration
Nate Smith, Kinfolk

jury.text: Full style review: swing, brushes, Latin, funk, odd meter
Present the 3-song demo
Recital program approved (by teacher or self-review)

goals: Show range: swing, brushes, Latin, funk, odd meter, original

items.text: Weekly run-throughs of the full program
Book a venue, band, and date
Preview performance for friends or teacher
Fix issues from the preview
Perform the recital
Record and archive it

musicianship.text: Write program notes for each tune

listening: Re-listen to every album from Semester 0. Notice what you hear now.

jury.text: Senior recital performed and recorded
